## Context / Problem

The current tests inspect replacement mechanics or final JSON rather than the write window (`test_applier_mapping.py:235-282`, `test_applier_provenance.py:155-185`), permit last-writer record loss (`test_bridge_state_atomic_write_concurrency.py:41-120`), and source-grep impossible-link durability (`test_impossible_links_cicada.py:467-493`). Live sidecars replace full snapshots in `peer_confirmations.py:192-217` and `impossible_links.py:376-401`.

## Approach

Use the existing locked store boundary for read-merge-write. Preserve distinct keys under concurrent writers, choose and document deterministic same-key resolution, and prove readers see either the old complete document or the new complete document. Verify real commit-back through a fresh store/read rather than source inspection.

## Scope

- reconciliation mapping, peer-confirmation, and impossible-link sidecar writers
- atomic persistence helpers
- focused concurrency, mapping, provenance, and durability tests

## Testing

Use barriers for two writers and an in-window reader; cover distinct keys, same key, malformed intermediate data, commit-back, and a fresh-reader control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Concurrent writes for distinct sidecar keys retain both records.
- [ ] Same-key conflict resolution is deterministic and covered by an explicit test.
- [ ] A barrier reader observes only the complete old or complete new state, never partial JSON.
- [ ] Mapping, peer-confirmation, and impossible-link writes use the common locked read-merge-write path.
- [ ] A fresh store/read proves committed impossible-link and mapping state survives publication.
